title: Deriving the Sine Difference Formula from the Sum Formula
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Use the sine addition formula \sin(A + B) = \sin A \cos B + \cos A \sin B together with even/odd identities to derive the difference formula \sin(A - B) = \sin A \cos B - \cos A \sin B.

steps.title: Substitute -B for B in the Sine Addition Formula
steps.explanation: Write A - B as A + (-B) and expand using sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B.
steps.why: The sine addition identity applies to all real angles.

steps.title: Apply Evenness of Cosine and Oddness of Sine
steps.explanation: Replace cos(-B) with cos B and sin(-B) with -sin B.
steps.why: Cosine is an even function and sine is an odd function.

steps.title: Simplify the Resulting Expression
steps.mathExpression: \sin(A - B) = \sin A \cos B + \cos A (-\sin B) = \sin A \cos B - \cos A \sin B
steps.explanation: Factor out the negative sign from the second term to complete the derivation.
steps.why: Adding cos A (-sin B) is algebraically equivalent to subtracting cos A sin B.
